content:
Reports indicate that Apple is taking a new approach to introducing artificial intelligence features for users in China: with the assistance of Alibaba, it is independently training a large language model.

According to a Reuters report, three sources described this China-exclusive model as a move by Apple to deviate from its long-standing strategy of relying on third-party models.

It is reported that Alibaba assisted in training the model, though neither company has responded to requests for comment.

Multiple models, including ChatGPT and Claude, are unavailable in mainland China, making Apple's current strategy in China differ from the approach it adopts in other major markets.

This development predates Alibaba's confirmation of its partnership with Apple in February 2025. Recently, Chinese internet regulators have also registered Apple Intelligence, permitting its use on the iPhone.

Previous reports indicated that Alibaba's Qwen model and Baidu's technology would be integrated into this localised system.

Reuters noted that it remains unclear how Apple's new model will work alongside these third-party models. The report stated that Apple Intelligence is expected to launch in China in the coming months following an iOS update.

Separately, Apple's significantly revamped Siri AI features are expected to be publicly released this autumn with iOS 27, limited to regions where the service is available.

Initially, support will be available for select English-language versions, while the rollout on iPhone and iPad in the European Union will be delayed. The launch timing for China has yet to be determined.
